functional-dependency.title: Functional Dependency
functional-dependency.last_question: What is the difference between partial and transitive dependency?
functional-dependency.last_answer: A partial dependency is a non-key attribute depending on part of a composite key; a transitive dependency is a non-key attribute depending on another non-key attribute.

dbms-unit-1:normalization-overview.title: Database Normalization Overview
dbms-unit-1:normalization-overview.last_question: What two main problems does database normalization aim to solve?
dbms-unit-1:normalization-overview.last_answer: To reduce duplication and improve data integrity.

java-introduction-5-pages:java-features.title: Key Features of Java
java-introduction-5-pages:java-features.last_question: What component is responsible for automatically reclaiming memory occupied by objects no longer in use?
java-introduction-5-pages:java-features.last_answer: The garbage collector (part of automatic memory management).

java-introduction-5-pages:java-workflow.title: How Java Works: JDK, JRE, JVM, and Bytecode
java-introduction-5-pages:java-workflow.last_question: In the standard Java workflow, what is produced after compiling a '.java' source file?

java-introduction-5-pages:java-fundament.title: Java Fundamentals: Variables, Operators, Control Flow
java-introduction-5-pages:java-fundament.last_question: When would you typically use a 'for' loop in Java?
java-introduction-5-pages:java-fundament.last_answer: When the number of repetitions is known in advance.

java-introduction-5-pages:java-oop.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Java
java-introduction-5-pages:java-oop.last_question: What distinguishes a Java constructor from a regular method?
java-introduction-5-pages:java-oop.last_answer: A constructor has the same name as its class and does not declare a return type.

java-introduction-5-pages:java-exception.title: Exception Handling in Java
java-introduction-5-pages:java-exception.last_question: What keyword is used in Java to define a block of code that handles a specific type of exception?

java-introduction-5-pages:java-collectio.title: Arrays and the Collections Framework
java-introduction-5-pages:java-collectio.last_question: Which interface from the Java Collections Framework is designed to store key-value pairs?

java-introduction-5-pages:java-practices.title: Good Programming Practices
java-introduction-5-pages:java-practices.last_question: What is one important good programming practice regarding comments?
java-introduction-5-pages:java-practices.last_answer: Use comments to explain why a decision was made, not merely to repeat what the code does.

java_intro:T1.title: Introduction to Java
java_intro:T1.last_question: What are two main advantages of Java's design compared to C/C++?
java_intro:T1.last_answer: Automatic memory management (garbage collection) and avoidance of some low-level operations.

java_intro:T2.title: Key Java Features & Components
java_intro:T2.last_question: Describe the typical workflow for developing and running a Java program using the JDK and JVM.
java_intro:T2.last_answer: Write source code in a .java file, compile it with 'javac' into bytecode (.class file), and then run the bytecode on a JVM.

java_intro:T6.title: First Java Program & Execution
java_intro:T6.last_question: What does String[] args in the main method represent?
java_intro:T6.last_answer: It receives command-line arguments passed to the program.

java_intro:T3.title: Java Basics: Variables, Operators & Control Flow
java_intro:T3.last_question: What is the primary difference between a while loop and a do-while loop?
java_intro:T3.last_answer: A 'do-while' loop executes its body at least once, whereas a 'while' loop may not execute at all if the condition is initially false.

java_intro:T4.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Java
java_intro:T4.last_question: What is the main difference between a method and a constructor?
java_intro:T4.last_answer: A method performs a task and may return a value, while a constructor initializes a new object and has no return type.

java_intro:T5.title: Advanced Java Concepts & Best Practices
java_intro:T5.last_question: Name two good programming practices mentioned in the lecture.
java_intro:T5.last_answer: Choose meaningful names, indent code consistently, use comments to explain 'why', validate input, prefer clear solutions, test thoroughly, use version control. (Any two of these)

java-continuation-part-2:method-basics.title: Methods in Java
java-continuation-part-2:method-basics.last_question: Why is changing only the return type not sufficient for method overloading?
java-continuation-part-2:method-basics.last_answer: Method overloading requires differences in the number, types, or order of parameters. The return type alone does not differentiate the method signature for the compiler.

java-continuation-part-2:strings-scanner.title: Strings and Keyboard Input
java-continuation-part-2:strings-scanner.last_question: What is a common issue when mixing `nextInt()` and `nextLine()` with `Scanner`, and how can it be resolved?
java-continuation-part-2:strings-scanner.last_answer: `nextInt()` (and similar methods) leaves the line break character in the input buffer, which `nextLine()` might consume immediately, resulting in an empty string. This can be resolved by adding an extra `sc.nextLine()` call to consume the leftover line break.

java-continuation-part-2:inheritance-pol.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
java-continuation-part-2:inheritance-pol.last_question: What are the three main uses of the `final` keyword in Java related to classes, methods, and variables?
java-continuation-part-2:inheritance-pol.last_answer: When applied to a class, it prevents inheritance. When applied to a method, it prevents overriding. When applied to a variable, it prevents reassignment (makes it a constant).

java-continuation-part-2:abstract-interf.title: Abstract Classes and Interfaces
java-continuation-part-2:abstract-interf.last_question: Can a Java class implement multiple interfaces? If so, what does this allow?
java-continuation-part-2:abstract-interf.last_answer: Yes, a class can implement multiple interfaces. This allows the class to adhere to multiple distinct contracts, gaining different sets of shared capabilities.

java-continuation-part-2:access-modifier.title: Access Modifiers
java-continuation-part-2:access-modifier.last_question: Describe the access level provided by the `protected` modifier.
java-continuation-part-2:access-modifier.last_answer: `protected` members are accessible within the same package and also by subclasses (through inheritance), even if those subclasses are in different packages.

java-continuation-part-2:packages-static.title: Packages and Static Members
java-continuation-part-2:packages-static.last_question: Why can't a `static` method directly access a non-`static` (instance) field without an object reference?
java-continuation-part-2:packages-static.last_answer: A static method belongs to the class itself and exists even if no objects of the class have been created. Instance fields belong to specific objects, so without an object reference, a static method wouldn't know which instance's field to access.

java-continuation-part-3:EXCP001.title: Exception Handling in Java
java-continuation-part-3:EXCP001.last_question: When would you use throw versus throws?
java-continuation-part-3:EXCP001.last_answer: throw is used to explicitly throw an exception object within a method body. throws is used in a method signature to declare that a method might throw certain checked exceptions.

java-continuation-part-3:COLL001.title: Java Collections Framework
java-continuation-part-3:COLL001.last_question: How does a Map differ from a Collection in Java's Collections Framework?
java-continuation-part-3:COLL001.last_answer: A Map stores key-value pairs and is not a direct subtype of Collection. Collection represents a group of objects, whereas Map represents a mapping from keys to values.

java-continuation-part-3:GENS001.title: Generics and Type Safety
java-continuation-part-3:GENS001.last_question: Describe how generics help prevent ClassCastException at runtime.
java-continuation-part-3:GENS001.last_answer: Generics enforce type checks at compile-time. If a program attempts to add an incorrect type to a generic collection (e.g., an Integer to List<String>), the compiler will flag it as an error, preventing a runtime ClassCastException.

java-continuation-part-3:FILE001.title: Basic File I/O
java-continuation-part-3:FILE001.last_question: Why is it important to handle IOException when performing file operations?
java-continuation-part-3:FILE001.last_answer: IOException is a checked exception, meaning the compiler requires it to be caught or declared. This ensures that potential issues during file operations (like file not found, permission denied, etc.) are explicitly addressed by the programmer.

java-continuation-part-3:MULT001.title: Multithreading Concepts
java-continuation-part-3:MULT001.last_question: What potential issue arises when multiple threads access and modify the same shared data?
java-continuation-part-3:MULT001.last_answer: Race conditions, data corruption, or inconsistent results due to lack of proper synchronization and coordination between threads.
